summary: Submitted sourced research feedback recording a newly found contract-versus-implementation discrepancy, with three new SourceRanges: S-snapshot-list-contract (snapshot.go:52-54, the SnapshotStore interface stating that List returns snapshots in descending order with the highest index first), S-file-snapshot-list (file_snapshot.go:226-290, List/getSnapshots computing the order via sort.Reverse(snapMetaSlice)), and S-file-snapshot-sort (file_snapshot.go:539-547, Less comparing Term before Index). The discrepancy: for two retained snapshots whose positions are inversely ordered (e.g. a local snapshot at (term 9, index 50) alongside one installed from a leader at (term 4, index 80)), the reversed term-first ordering returns the lower-index snapshot first, contradicting the documented contract. Two consumers select element zero to choose state - the leader's sendLatestSnapshot ships snapshots[0] to a lagging follower, and NewRaft's restoreSnapshot restores the first snapshot that loads - which is why the ordering is behaviourally significant for recovery. No defect is presumed and no map change is proposed: the remaining unknowns fix the discriminator (whether inversely ordered retained snapshots can coexist, whether restoring the lower-index snapshot regresses applied state or fails the startup scan, and whether term-first is an intentional authority ordering that merely disagrees with the interface wording). This turn's earlier second-scenario review for C-append-log-identity-consistency was accepted with a complete violated witness (cached_index 3 vs stored_index 2, probe rejected), so the run still has three confirmed findings. Preflight returned valid:true.
